# Introduction
- This poster explores how race and socio-economic background predict future income outcomes in the U.S.
- Using Opportunity Insights data, we evaluate correlations between race, parental income, and adult income rank.
- Statistical and machine learning models are used to evaluate predictive performance.

# Methods
- Data: U.S. Census Public Use Data from Opportunity Insights
- Sample size: 64 observations
- Key variables: `par_pctile`, `count_black_pooled`, `kir_1par_black_male`, `kir_1par_white_male`

$$
IncomeRank = f(ParentIncome, BlackPopulation)
$$

# Results

## CDF of Parent Percentile
The CDF plot of parent income percentile shows a near-perfect linear increase, indicating a uniform distribution across socio-economic statuses.

```{r cdf-plot, fig.cap='CDF of Parent Income Percentile'}
ggplot(data, aes(x = par_pctile)) +
  stat_ecdf(geom = "step", color = "blue") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Histogram of Black Population Count
The histogram is skewed towards lower Black population counts, with peaks at lower counts, suggesting racial segregation patterns.

```{r histogram-black-count, fig.cap='Histogram of Black Population Count'}
ggplot(data, aes(x = count_black_pooled)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5000, fill = "green", color = "black") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Scatter Plot with Regression
Higher Black population counts correlate negatively with income ranks for Black males from single-parent households, highlighting systemic disparities.

```{r scatter-black-kir, fig.cap='Black Count vs. Economic Outcome (Black Males, 1 Parent)'} 
ggplot(data, aes(x = count_black_pooled, y = kir_1par_black_male)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Correlation Matrix
Parental income percentile is positively correlated with economic outcomes, whereas Black population size is negatively correlated.

```{r correlation-matrix}
cor_matrix <- cor(data[, c("par_pctile", "count_black_pooled", "kir_1par_black_male", "kir_1par_white_male")])
knitr::kable(cor_matrix, caption = "Correlation Matrix of Key Variables")
```

## Predictive Modeling (KNN)
The KNN model (k=5) achieves an RMSE of 1.078 and an R-squared of 0.962, suggesting strong predictive capacity based on only two predictors.

```{r knn-model}
predictors <- c("par_pctile", "count_black_pooled")
target <- "kir_1par_black_male"

set.seed(123)
trainIndex <- createDataPartition(data[[target]], p = .8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- data[trainIndex, ]
test_data <- data[-trainIndex, ]

control <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 10)
knn_fit <- train(as.formula(paste(target, "~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + "))),
                 data = train_data,
                 method = "knn",
                 trControl = control,
                 metric = "RMSE")

knn_predictions <- predict(knn_fit, newdata = test_data)
knn_rmse <- sqrt(mean((knn_predictions - test_data[[target]])^2))
knn_r2 <- cor(knn_predictions, test_data[[target]])^2

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Metric = c("RMSE", "R-squared"),
    Value = c(round(knn_rmse, 3), round(knn_r2, 3))
  ),
  caption = "KNN Model Performance"
)
```
